title: Sparse density mode and column reflow heuristics for ultra-wide virtual tables
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background:
We have many tickets addressing column resizing, density presets, and virtualized rendering. A recurring problem remains when customers with very wide tables (50+ columns) try to balance visibility and interaction fidelity. Current density modes only toggle row height and padding; they don't address selective column compression or the UX signals needed when columns are dynamically reflowed by the runtime.

Goal:
Introduce a 'sparse density' mode and a set of deterministic column reflow heuristics so that ultra-wide virtual tables: (1) remain performant under virtualization, (2) preserve important columns using priority mappings, (3) provide predictable resizing affordances and visual anchors (ghost rulers) that help users orient when columns collapse/expand, and (4) are fully keyboard- and screen-reader accessible.

Scope / Non-scope:
- In scope: design tokens for sparse density (padding/typography), visual indicators (ghost rulers / sticky reflow rails), column priority mapping UI, microinteractions for progressive column collapse and unobtrusive tooltips, keyboard flows and ARIA announcements, updated responsive rules for column compression.
- Out of scope for this ticket: full runtime implementation of compression algorithms (tracked in ENG-20712), server-side rollups for column summaries, and analytics ingestion pipeline (separate instrumentation ticket).

Design principles and constraints:
- Determinism: given the same table width and priorities, ordering and collapsed state must be reproducible across sessions.
- Minimal layout shift: prefer progressive reveal over sudden jumps; use transform-based animations where possible.
- Performance-first: designs should avoid per-cell heavy DOM changes; prioritize the virtualization layer to manage rendering boundaries.
- Accessibility: ensure focus retention when columns collapse, and provide clear spoken updates about column compression state.

Key deliverables:
1) Token set for sparse density (rowHeight, cellPadding, iconSize, collapseCueColor) and example token mappings.
2) Visual spec for 'ghost rulers' (thin sticky guides at collapse boundaries) and 'reflow rail' for drag interactions.
3) Interaction spec for manual resize in sparse mode: snap thresholds, compression preview overlay, multi-column drag behavior, and keyboard +/- column width controls.
4) ARIA/Screen-reader spec: announcements, focus management, and fallback flows.
5) Prototype (Figma + interactive HTML prototype) demonstrating a 60-column table with priority mapping and progressive compression.
6) Acceptance criteria and QA checklist for engineering handoff.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sparse density token set implemented in design library and documented.
- Prototype demonstrates deterministic reflow for three width breakpoints and exposes a UI to set column priority.
- Interaction spec covers mouse, touch, and keyboard; includes animation timing and accessible text.
- Engineering partner (ENG-20712) confirms feasibility for virtualization runtime integration without violating 16ms frame budget for common workloads.
- PM approves rollout plan and can map feature flags for gradual release.

Metrics to monitor after rollout:
- Mean frame render time for wide tables (target < 20ms median).
- Frequency of manual user resizes in sparse mode (expect downshift vs baseline).
- Accessibility regressions: automated axe checks and user validation with screen-reader flows.

Notes on tradeoffs:
- We intentionally avoid auto-hiding columns entirely (that's a destructive change for users). Instead, compression reduces padding and hides non-critical affordances (icons/secondary metadata) while keeping primary content visible. This accepts slightly increased cognitive load to preserve data integrity.
- Ghost rulers are a light-weight visual anchor; we tested heavier overlays in prototypes and they blocked interaction.

Handoff expectations:
- Provide tokens + Figma components + an HTML prototype repo link.
- A short walkthrough video (2–3 minutes) to accompany the handoff.
- Open questions for engineering: exact compression algorithm, how to persist user overrides, and analytics payload format.
